title: Absconding to avoid service of summons or other proceeding
old_text: Penalized absconding to avoid service of summons with simple imprisonment up to 1 month or fine up to ₹500; if summons from court of justice, up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1,000.
new_text: Whoever absconds in order to avoid being served with a summons, notice or order proceeding from any public servant legally competent to issue the same, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; if from a Court of Justice, with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both.
punishment_old: General: up to 1 month or fine ₹500; Court of justice: up to 6 months or fine ₹1,000 (IPC Section 172).
punishment_new: General: up to 1 month or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; Court of Justice: up to 6 months or fine up to ₹10,000, or both (BNS Section 206).
explanation: Penalizes evading or absconding from official summons and judicial notices, increasing statutory fine limits tenfold. Renumbered from IPC Section 172.

title: Preventing service of summons or other proceeding, or preventing publication thereof
old_text: Penalized intentionally preventing service or publication of summons with simple imprisonment up to 1 month or fine up to ₹500; from Court, up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1,000.
new_text: Whoever intentionally prevents the serving on himself or another of any summons, notice or order, or prevents lawful affixing or publication thereof, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; if from a Court of Justice, up to six months, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both.
punishment_old: General: up to 1 month or fine ₹500; Court of justice: up to 6 months or fine ₹1,000 (IPC Section 173).
punishment_new: General: up to 1 month or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; Court of Justice: up to 6 months or fine up to ₹10,000, or both (BNS Section 207).
explanation: Criminalizes tearing down, refusing delivery, or physically obstructing process servers delivering judicial notices. Renumbered from IPC Section 173.

title: Non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant
old_text: Penalized intentional non-attendance in obedience to summons from public servant with simple imprisonment up to 1 month or fine up to ₹500; from Court, up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1,000.
new_text: Whoever, being legally bound to attend in person or by agent in obedience to a summons, notice, or order from a public servant, intentionally omits to attend or departs before time, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; if from a Court of Justice, up to six months, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both.
punishment_old: General: up to 1 month or fine ₹500; Court: up to 6 months or fine ₹1,000 (IPC Section 174).
punishment_new: General: up to 1 month or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; Court of Justice: up to 6 months or fine up to ₹10,000, or both (BNS Section 208).
explanation: Penalizes failing to appear before investigative officers, tax authorities, or courts pursuant to lawful summons. Renumbered from IPC Section 174.

title: Non-appearance in response to a proclamation under section 84 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
old_text: Penalized failure to appear as required by proclamation under Section 82 of CrPC with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine; proclaimed offenders under serious crimes faced up to 7 years and fine.
new_text: Whoever fails to appear at the specified place and time required by a proclamation published under sub-section (1) of section 84 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both; and where proclaimed offender declaration is made under sub-section (4), with imprisonment up to seven years and fine.
punishment_old: Basic proclamation: up to 3 years or fine or both; Proclaimed offender: up to 7 years and fine (IPC Section 174A).
punishment_new: Basic proclamation: imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both; Proclaimed offender: imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine (BNS Section 209).
explanation: Punishes absconding proclaimed offenders who evade court appearances, referencing Section 84 of the newly enacted Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). Renumbered from IPC Section 174A.

title: Omission to produce document or electronic record to public servant by person legally bound to produce it
old_text: Penalized intentional omission to produce a document to a public servant with simple imprisonment up to 1 month or fine up to ₹500; to a Court, up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1,000.
new_text: Whoever, being legally bound to produce or deliver up any document or electronic record to any public servant, intentionally omits so to produce or deliver up the same, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; if to a Court of Justice, up to six months, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both.
punishment_old: General: up to 1 month or fine ₹500; Court: up to 6 months or fine ₹1,000 (IPC Section 175).
punishment_new: General: up to 1 month or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; Court of Justice: up to 6 months or fine up to ₹10,000, or both (BNS Section 210).
explanation: Penalizes withholding documents or electronic records from authorized public servants and courts, raising the fine limit tenfold. Renumbered from IPC Section 175.

title: Omission to give notice or information to public servant by person legally bound to give it
old_text: Penalized intentional omission to give notice or information legally required with simple imprisonment up to 1 month or fine up to ₹500; regarding offence commission, up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1,000.
new_text: Whoever, being legally bound to give any notice or information to any public servant, intentionally omits to give such notice or information, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; if relating to the commission of an offence, up to six months, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both.
punishment_old: General: up to 1 month or fine ₹500; Offence info: up to 6 months or fine ₹1,000 (IPC Section 176).
punishment_new: General: up to 1 month or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; Offence reporting: up to 6 months or fine up to ₹10,000, or both (BNS Section 211).
explanation: Penalizes failure to notify authorities where a statutory duty to inform exists (e.g. reporting serious felonies). Renumbered from IPC Section 176.

title: Furnishing false information
old_text: Penalized furnishing false information knowing it to be false with simple imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1,000; regarding offence commission, up to 2 years or fine.
new_text: Whoever, being legally bound to furnish information on any subject to any public servant, furnishes as true information which he knows or has reason to believe to be false, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; if relating to commission of an offence, with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: General: up to 6 months or fine ₹1,000; Offence related: up to 2 years or fine or both (IPC Section 177).
punishment_new: General: up to 6 months or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; Offence related: imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both (BNS Section 212).
explanation: Penalizes providing deceptive or fabricated information to government officers when under a legal duty to furnish facts. Renumbered from IPC Section 177.

title: Refusing oath or affirmation when duly required by public servant to make it
old_text: Penalized refusing to bind oneself by oath or affirmation when lawfully required with simple imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.
new_text: Whoever refuses to bind himself by an oath or affirmation to state the truth, when required so to bind himself by a public servant legally competent to require that he shall so bind himself, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
punishment_old: Simple imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both (IPC Section 178).
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both (BNS Section 213).
explanation: Penalizes witnesses or deponents who refuse to take an oath or affirmation before judicial or quasi-judicial tribunals. Renumbered from IPC Section 178.

title: Refusing to answer public servant authorised to question
old_text: Penalized refusing to answer questions put by a public servant legally authorized to question with simple imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.
new_text: Whoever, being legally bound to state the truth on any subject to any public servant, refuses to answer any question demanded of him touching that subject by such public servant in the exercise of legal powers, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both.
punishment_old: Simple imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both (IPC Section 179).
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both (BNS Section 214).
explanation: Penalizes recalcitrant witnesses who refuse to answer lawful inquiries during administrative or judicial investigations (subject to Article 20(3) self-incrimination safeguards). Renumbered from IPC Section 179.

title: Refusing to sign statement
old_text: Penalized refusing to sign a statement made to a public servant when legally required with simple imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to ₹500, or both.
new_text: Whoever refuses to sign any statement made by him, when required to sign that statement by a public servant legally competent to require that he shall sign that statement, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to three months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.
punishment_old: Simple imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹500, or both (IPC Section 180).
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both (BNS Section 215).
explanation: Penalizes refusing to sign depositions or recorded formal statements where the law mandates execution. Renumbered from IPC Section 180.

title: False statement on oath or affirmation to public servant or person authorised to administer an oath or affirmation
old_text: Penalized making false statements under oath or affirmation to a public servant with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.
new_text: Whoever, being legally bound by an oath or affirmation to state the truth on any subject to any public servant, makes any statement which is false, and which he knows or believes to be false, shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, and fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 3 years, and fine (IPC Section 181).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to three years, and shall also be liable to fine (BNS Section 216).
explanation: Penalizes perjury and swearing false affidavits before public functionaries authorized to administer oaths. Renumbered from IPC Section 181.

title: False information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to injury of another person
old_text: Penalized giving false information to a public servant intending to cause them to use lawful power to the injury or annoyance of another with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.
new_text: Whoever gives to any public servant any information which he knows or believes to be false, intending thereby to cause such public servant to use his lawful power to cause injury or annoyance to any person, shall be punished with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both (IPC Section 182).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to six months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both (BNS Section 217).
explanation: Penalizes filing fabricated police complaints or malicious reports designed to weaponize law enforcement against innocent rivals, raising the fine tenfold. Renumbered from IPC Section 182.

title: Resistance to taking of property by lawful authority of a public servant
old_text: Penalized resisting the attachment or taking of property under lawful authority of a public servant with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.
new_text: Whoever offers any resistance to the taking of any property by the lawful authority of any public servant, knowing or having reason to believe that he is such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both (IPC Section 183).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both (BNS Section 218).
explanation: Penalizes resisting bailiffs or tax collectors carrying out lawful court attachments or property seizures. Renumbered from IPC Section 183.

title: Obstructing sale of property offered for sale by authority of public servant
old_text: Penalized intentionally obstructing public auctions of property conducted under authority of a public servant with imprisonment up to 1 month or fine up to ₹500, or both.
new_text: Whoever intentionally obstructs any sale of property offered for sale by the lawful authority of any public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment up to one month, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to ₹500, or both (IPC Section 184).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to one month, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both (BNS Section 219).
explanation: Protects public revenue and judicial recovery auctions against disruptions and physical obstruction. Renumbered from IPC Section 184.

title: Illegal purchase or bid for property offered for sale by authority of public servant
old_text: Penalized bidding for property when under legal incapacity, or bidding without intention to perform obligations, with imprisonment up to 1 month or fine up to ₹200, or both.
new_text: Whoever, at any sale of property held by authority of a public servant, bids for property under legal incapacity to purchase, or bids without intending to perform the obligations incurred, shall be punished with imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to ₹200, or both (IPC Section 185).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to one month, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both (BNS Section 220).
explanation: Penalizes sham bidding and cartel rigging at court auctions by parties legally barred or having no intention to pay. Renumbered from IPC Section 185.

title: Obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions
old_text: Penalized voluntarily obstructing a public servant in discharge of public functions with imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to ₹500, or both.
new_text: Whoever voluntarily obstructs any public servant in the discharge of his public functions, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹500, or both (IPC Section 186).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to three months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both (BNS Section 221).
explanation: Core statutory shield penalizing physical or administrative obstruction of civil servants performing lawful duties, raising the maximum fine from ₹500 to ₹5,000. Renumbered from IPC Section 186.

title: Omission to assist public servant when bound by law to give assistance
old_text: Penalized omitting to assist a public servant when legally bound to assist with simple imprisonment up to 1 month or fine up to ₹200; if for executing process or suppressing riot, up to 6 months or fine up to ₹500.
new_text: Whoever, being bound by law to render or furnish assistance to any public servant in the execution of his duty, intentionally omits to give such assistance, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to ₹2,500, or both; if assistance is demanded to execute legal process or suppress riot/affray, up to six months, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both.
punishment_old: General: up to 1 month or fine ₹200; Process/riot: up to 6 months or fine ₹500 (IPC Section 187).
punishment_new: General: up to 1 month or fine up to ₹2,500, or both; Legal process / riot suppression: up to 6 months or fine up to ₹5,000, or both (BNS Section 222).
explanation: Enforces civic duty to assist police and public officers in apprehending criminals or quelling riots when legally called upon. Renumbered from IPC Section 187.

title: Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant
old_text: Penalized disobedience to orders promulgated by public servants (e.g. Section 144 orders) with simple imprisonment up to 1 month or fine up to ₹200; if causing danger to life/health, up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1,000.
new_text: Whoever, knowing that an order has been promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered to direct abstention from a certain act, disobeys such direction, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to ₹2,500, or both; and if disobedience causes danger to human life, health or safety, or causes a riot, with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both.
punishment_old: General: up to 1 month or fine ₹200; Endangering life/riot: up to 6 months or fine ₹1,000 (IPC Section 188).
punishment_new: General: simple imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to ₹2,500, or both; Endangering life/health/riot: imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both (BNS Section 223).
explanation: Penalizes violating curfew, prohibitory assembly orders, or public health directives promulgated by district magistrates, raising statutory fine ceilings. Renumbered from IPC Section 188.

title: Threat of injury to public servant
old_text: Penalized holding out any threat of injury to a public servant to induce them to do or forbear any official act with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever holds out any threat of injury to any public servant, or to any person in whom he believes that public servant to be interested, for the purpose of inducing that public servant to do any act, or to forbear or delay any act connected with the exercise of his public functions, shall be punished with imprisonment up to two years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or with fine, or with both (IPC Section 189).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 224).
explanation: Protects public officials against blackmail, physical threats, or harassment aimed at derailing official enforcement actions. Renumbered from IPC Section 189.

title: Threat of injury to induce person to refrain from applying for protection to public servant
old_text: Penalized holding out threats of injury to induce any person to refrain from applying to a public servant for protection with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever holds out any threat of injury to any person for the purpose of inducing that person to refrain or desist from making a legal application for protection against any injury to any public servant legally empowered as such to give such protection, shall be punished with imprisonment up to one year, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 1 year, or with fine, or with both (IPC Section 190).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to one year, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 225).
explanation: Guarantees citizen access to justice and administrative remedy by penalizing intimidation designed to prevent victims from approaching police or magistrates. Renumbered from IPC Section 190.

title: Attempt to commit suicide to compel or restrain exercise of lawful power
old_text: None (General attempt to commit suicide under IPC Section 309 was rendered practically inoperative by the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017; no specific provision existed for blackmailing public servants via suicide threats).
new_text: Whoever attempts to commit suicide with the intent to compel or restrain any public servant from exercising his lawful power, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both, or with community service.
punishment_old: Not specifically codified in IPC.
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both, or with community service (BNS Section 226).
explanation: A major statutory innovation in the BNS. While ordinary suicide attempts are not penalized, Section 226 specifically criminalizes suicide attempts deployed as public blackmail (such as self-immolation or hunger strikes) to coerce or prevent public servants from executing lawful duties, including community service as an alternative sanction.
